title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). 𝔊 is a profinite group with a 'couple' (ρ,σ), ρ³=1, σ²=1. Equivalently, 𝔊 is a quotient of the profinite completion of Z/3 * Z/2 ≅ PSL(2,Z), the orbifold fundamental group of M_{1,1}. To such a pair Grothendieck attaches a family of groups:
- B_{ρ,σ}: a Borel-type group, the normaliser of the 'parabolic' procyclic subgroup L_0 = closure of ⟨ε_0⟩, ε_0 = σ^{-1}ρ;
- G_{ρ,σ} and S_0G_{ρ,σ}: groups of automorphisms compatible with the pair;
- Z_ρ, Z_σ: centraliser/normaliser-type groups of ρ and σ;
- Γ_{ρ,σ}, γ_{ρ,σ}: Galois/Teichmüller-type quotients;
- M_{ρ,σ}, S_0M_{ρ,σ}: 'multiplier' groups, made explicit in section III on the next page.

The universal case, (90)-(92). Here 𝔊 = 𝔖^{+∧}_{0,3}, universal for pairs with ρ³=σ²=1. The page records that the natural maps are isomorphisms:
- Γ' ≅ γ', Z'_ρ ≅ γ', Z'_σ ≅ γ';
- hence S_0M' ≅ S_0M^~_{0,3} and M' ≅ M^~_{0,3}, with the analogous statements for S_0G' and G' added interlineally;
- (92'): SZ'_ρ = SZ'_σ = SΓ'.
So in the universal case all these invariants collapse onto one Galois/GT-type group.

Remark on notation, (93). Writing relation (80) showed that the section II notation was inadequate. All of Σ, B, G, S_0G, γ, Z_ρ, Z_σ, Γ, SG, SZ, S_0M⁰, M⁰ get a prime, and the superscript ⁰ is replaced by the prime. The margin note says the old notation clashed with the modular case 𝔊 = SL(2,Ẑ) and with §53'.

Case 2°, the congruence (modular) case, (94). 𝔊 = SL(2,Ẑ)/±1, the congruence completion, with (ρ,σ) the standard modular pair of elements of order 3 and 2.
- B' = {(μ λ; 0 1) : μ ∈ Ẑ*, μ ≡ 1 mod 3, λ ∈ Ẑ}.
- L_0 is the unipotent group {(1 λ; 0 1)}.
- G' = GL'(2,Ẑ)/±1, where GL' = {u : det u ≡ 1 mod 3}. Margin: this is G(Ẑ)/μ_2 resp. Γ_0(Ẑ)/μ_2 in the group-scheme notation of §48.
- Z'_ρ = {cρ+d : c²+cd+d² ∈ Ẑ*}/±1, the unit group of Ẑ[ρ] ≅ Ẑ⊗Z[ζ_3]. This is the centraliser of ρ in GL_2(Ẑ).
- Z'_σ = N'_σ(Ẑ)/μ_2. The next page makes it explicit as (units of Ẑ[i])·{1, τ_∞}, with τ_∞ = diag(−1,1).
- S_0M', M', Γ' are given as Ẑ-points of group schemes from §48 (SM'_{ρσ}, M'_{ρσ}, T_{ρσ}) modulo finite groups Σ, Σ_0.

Why the condition 'mod 3'. Conjugation by an element of determinant d sends the class of ρ to that of ρ^{±1} according to d mod 3. Norms of units of Z_3[ζ_3] are ≡ 1 mod 3. So det ≡ 1 mod 3 is exactly the condition for respecting the conjugacy class of ρ itself, not of ρ^{-1}. It is the analogue of the cyclotomic character mod 3 that appears in the universal (GT/Galois) case.

Purpose. This is a test/comparison case. For the 'congruence shadow' of π_1(M_{1,1}), the GT-type group of compatible automorphisms becomes the explicit arithmetic group GL'(2,Ẑ)/±1. The next page then defines the 'cyclotomic' character χ: B' → Aut(L_0) ≅ (Ẑ/J)*, attached to n ↦ ε_0^n.
errors: Indexing is inconsistent in the universal-case isomorphisms: Z'_{ρ'} ≅ γ_{ρ',σ'} is written without a prime on γ, while Γ' ≅ γ' has one. These are notational slips, which the Remark itself acknowledges.

The norm form c²+cd+d² is the norm of cρ+d only if ρ is taken as the order-6 lift in SL_2, satisfying ρ²−ρ+1=0. For the order-3 lift it would be c²−cd+d². Both give the same unit group, so this is harmless.
B' and L_0 are written as matrices in GL_2 without dividing by ±1, although 𝔊 and G' are taken mod ±1. The matrices with lower-right entry 1 give a section, so this is not a real error.

ideas.what: In the universal case 𝔊 = completion of Z/3*Z/2, the various compatibility groups (Γ', Z'_ρ, Z'_σ, M', S_0M', G') all coincide with one Galois/GT-type group.
ideas.modern_name: GT-type group of automorphisms of π_1^orb(M_{1,1})^ preserving the inertia classes; rigidity of the (2,3) presentation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps (GT and its genus-1 / Γ_{1,1} variants)
ideas.where_published: The general philosophy is in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, M_{1,1}); these specific invariants appear unpublished.

ideas.what: Explicit determination, for the congruence completion PSL(2,Ẑ), of the group of compatible automorphisms: GL'(2,Ẑ)/±1 with det ≡ 1 mod 3, and Borel B' with μ ≡ 1 mod 3.
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of the congruence completion preserving the conjugacy classes of elliptic elements; the Galois action on the congruence quotient factoring through the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (e.g. Galois action on the modular tower via det/cyclotomic character; Ihara, Nakamura and others)

ideas.what: Centralisers of the elliptic elements as unit groups of Ẑ[ζ_3] and of Ẑ[i] (extended by τ_∞).
ideas.modern_name: Profinite CM tori attached to the elliptic points j=0, j=1728

ideas.what: A uniform functorial package of invariants (B, G, Z_ρ, Z_σ, Γ, M, S_0M) attached to any quotient of Z/3*Z/2 with marked generators, compared across quotients.
ideas.modern_name: Close to 'GT-shadows' for finite quotients (Dolgushev et al.) and to Galois/GT actions on dessins (Schneps, Lochak)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, for an arbitrary profinite quotient 𝔊 of Z/3*Z/2 with marked (ρ,σ), a system of 'compatibility' groups. He computes it both in the universal case (where it collapses to the GT/Galois-type group) and in congruence quotients (where it becomes GL'(2,Ẑ)/±1). This is structurally the idea later developed as 'GT-shadows' of finite quotients, here in the M_{1,1}/(2,3) setting rather than the M_{0,4}/PB_4 setting.
missed.quote: Autres cas particuliers importants ... 2°) 𝔊 = Sl(2,Ẑ)/±1, (ρ,σ) couple modulaire ... G'_{ρ,σ} = Gl'(2,Ẑ)/±1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a genus-1, (2,3)-analogue of the GT-shadow programme, with explicitly computed test cases. It could inform 'modular GT-shadows' for congruence and non-congruence quotients of PSL_2(Z).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly notational housekeeping plus a fairly routine explicit computation of the congruence case. The interest lies in the framework, which anticipates GT-shadow-type comparisons across quotients of π_1(M_{1,1}). The individual results are standard.
transcription_corrections: The line with S_0M' ≅ S_0M^~_{0,3} appears to be labelled (91) in the left margin, not (92). The top-left marginal block is labelled (92') and reads SZ'_{ρ'} = SZ'_{σ'} = SΓ'_{ρ',σ'}.
'564' is a cross-reference inserted above the first line.
The marginal note on the left of the Remarques roughly reads: 'car V_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) ... était, en cas 𝔊 = Sl(2,Ẑ), ... cas modulaire ... cf. § 53' ... 𝔊_{ρ,σ} ... aurait dû ... ces notations'.
The left margin next to G'_{ρ,σ} reads 'c'est G(Ẑ)/μ_2(Z) avec notations du § 48'. Next to the definition of Gl' it reads '≃ Γ_0(Ẑ)/μ_2(Z)'; a crossed-out version of that note sits below it.
In (94) the last line is Γ'_{ρ,σ} ≃ T_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ_0, preceded by M'_{ρ,σ} ≃ M'_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ 'id'.
